claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked: counter vectors Fin k -> Nat under pointwise sum form a commutative cancellative monoid that is not a group (every nonzero vector lacks an inverse) and is the free commutative monoid on k ids (universal property, existence and uniqueness); the bounded combine that refuses past a count bound is partially associative with equal definedness on both bracketings, and bounded generation returns none exactly when some coordinate would exceed the bound (genB_none_iff); the re-declared copy (Ev, evOb, trace) of the source three-counter trace is a monoid homomorphism from lists of the four declared events; coordinate 0 counts declareTerm, coordinate 1 counts assertDiff, coordinate 2 counts removeDiff plus identifyTerms together, and the total equals the list length; the copy is order-blind and its event table is not injective; one discharge step from a valid ledger yields a valid ledger and succeeds exactly when the request is at most the outstanding count, and, for the unbounded k-id model with generate and discharge operations, every successful run from the empty ledger ends valid (run_from_empty_valid). Native: exact tables for 34 cases (laws on boxes up to 3 ids x 4, bounded and saturating sums, 13 event words, 12 ledger traces over three ids with u64 bound covering every error kind and a generation landing exactly on 2^64-1); the native ledger is a model of the Rust rule, not the Rust crate.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: That Genesis events or S(n) maps are monoid morphisms into the obligation monoid (TFQ-0342, PG-GAP-EVENT-OBLIGATION): the event-to-vector table evOb is copied from the source, not derived, and only lists of the four declared events are covered; any theorem tying Ev/evOb/trace to PrimGenEvent/eventObligation/traceObligation of DerivationDagQMClosure.lean (they are a re-declaration); any theorem connecting the Lean abstract-k unbounded ledger to the three-id u64 Python/Rust ledger; the Rust crate itself (nothing in omega_kernel is executed); unbounded or string-keyed ids; any claim that the 3-counter vector equals the free monoid on the real obligation ids.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: Obligation counters under pointwise sum are the free commutative monoid on the ids (cancellative, not a group); the re-declared copy of the source four-event three-counter trace is a homomorphism from event lists with total cost equal to length; in the abstract unbounded k-id model every successful generate/discharge run from the empty ledger keeps discharged within generated and a discharge succeeds exactly when it fits the outstanding count; Genesis events and S(n) maps being morphisms remains unproved.
claim_boundary.next_test: Derive from the actual Genesis event and S(n)-map definitions (not the four-event table) that each step adds a fixed generated and discharged vector independent of context, i.e. that sequential composition maps to combine, or exhibit an event whose vector depends on the preceding trace.

report:
# PG-OBLIGATION-MONOID

Read DerivationDagQMClosure.lean lines 6-56 (sha c9ad9c23a4) and obligation.rs (sha 172ab7d7cb, matches the pin). The source Lean ObligationMonoid is a Nat triple with componentwise add; traceObligation_append is a correct general list-append lemma. declare_then_assert_cost_floor is the arithmetic fact that two counters >= 1 sum to >= 2: its hypothesis ValidFreshAssertionTrace does not order declare before assert. The Rust Obligations is described as the free commutative monoid in a doc comment only; no universal property is stated. The node states that Genesis morphisms are meant to carry these vectors: this bundle proves the monoid facts, the free-monoid property, the declared-event trace homomorphism and the ledger rule, and does not prove the Genesis/S(n) morphism claim, as TFQ-0342 requires. Found: the monoid is cancellative and not a group (not a failure of cancellation as one might fear), the saturating alternative fails cancellation, the event table loses order and identifies two events.

Supported: Kernel-checked: counter vectors Fin k -> Nat under pointwise sum form a commutative cancellative monoid that is not a group (every nonzero vector lacks an inverse) and is the free commutative monoid on k ids (universal property, existence and uniqueness); the bounded combine that refuses past a count bound is partially associative with equal definedness on both bracketings, and bounded generation returns none exactly when some coordinate would exceed the bound (genB_none_iff); the re-declared copy (Ev, evOb, trace) of the source three-counter trace is a monoid homomorphism from lists of the four declared events; coordinate 0 counts declareTerm, coordinate 1 counts assertDiff, coordinate 2 counts removeDiff plus identifyTerms together, and the total equals the list length; the copy is order-blind and its event table is not injective; one discharge step from a valid ledger yields a valid ledger and succeeds exactly when the request is at most the outstanding count, and, for the unbounded k-id model with generate and discharge operations, every successful run from the empty ledger ends valid (run_from_empty_valid). Native: exact tables for 34 cases (laws on boxes up to 3 ids x 4, bounded and saturating sums, 13 event words, 12 ledger traces over three ids with u64 bound covering every error kind and a generation landing exactly on 2^64-1); the native ledger is a model of the Rust rule, not the Rust crate.

Remaining: That Genesis events or S(n) maps are monoid morphisms into the obligation monoid (TFQ-0342, PG-GAP-EVENT-OBLIGATION): the event-to-vector table evOb is copied from the source, not derived, and only lists of the four declared events are covered; any theorem tying Ev/evOb/trace to PrimGenEvent/eventObligation/traceObligation of DerivationDagQMClosure.lean (they are a re-declaration); any theorem connecting the Lean abstract-k unbounded ledger to the three-id u64 Python/Rust ledger; the Rust crate itself (nothing in omega_kernel is executed); unbounded or string-keyed ids; any claim that the 3-counter vector equals the free monoid on the real obligation ids.
construction: Exhaustive tables on counter boxes, bounded and saturating sums, event words and ledger traces; Lean proves the general statements for every k.
